cards.front: dissolve
cards.back: When a solid mixes into a liquid and seems to disappear, making a clear mixture called a solution.
cards.say: dissolve. When a solid mixes into a liquid and seems to disappear, making a clear mixture called a solution.

cards.front: solute
cards.back: The substance that dissolves, such as the salt in salty water.
cards.say: solute. The substance that dissolves, such as the salt in salty water.

cards.front: solvent
cards.back: The liquid that does the dissolving, such as the water in salty water.
cards.say: solvent. The liquid that does the dissolving, such as the water in salty water.

cards.front: solution
cards.back: A mixture made when a solute has dissolved in a solvent.
cards.say: solution. A mixture made when a solute has dissolved in a solvent.

cards.front: soluble
cards.back: Able to dissolve in a liquid. Sugar is soluble in water.
cards.say: soluble. Able to dissolve in a liquid. Sugar is soluble in water.

cards.front: insoluble
cards.back: Not able to dissolve in a liquid. Sand is insoluble in water.
cards.say: insoluble. Not able to dissolve in a liquid. Sand is insoluble in water.

cards.front: Is salt soluble or insoluble in water?
cards.back: Soluble. It dissolves to make salty water.
cards.say: Is salt soluble or insoluble in water? Soluble. It dissolves to make salty water.

cards.front: Is sand soluble or insoluble in water?
cards.back: Insoluble. It stays as grains and sinks to the bottom.
cards.say: Is sand soluble or insoluble in water? Insoluble. It stays as grains and sinks to the bottom.

cards.front: Is a salt solution clear or cloudy?
cards.back: Clear. You can see through it, although it may be coloured.
cards.say: Is a salt solution clear or cloudy? Clear. You can see through it, although it may be coloured.

cards.front: When sugar dissolves in water, has it gone for ever?
cards.back: No. Its tiny particles have spread out between the water particles. You can still taste the sugar.
cards.say: When sugar dissolves in water, has it gone for ever? No. Its tiny particles have spread out between the water particles. You can still taste the sugar.

cards.front: Fifty grams of water and ten grams of sugar are mixed and the sugar dissolves. What is the mass of the solution?
cards.back: Sixty grams. No matter is lost when something dissolves.
cards.say: Fifty grams of water and ten grams of sugar are mixed and the sugar dissolves. What is the mass of the solution? Sixty grams. No matter is lost when something dissolves.

cards.front: Name three ways to make a solid dissolve faster.
cards.back: Stir it, use warmer water, or break the solid into smaller pieces.
cards.say: Name three ways to make a solid dissolve faster. Stir it, use warmer water, or break the solid into smaller pieces.

cards.front: Why does warmer water dissolve a solid faster?
cards.back: Its particles move faster and hit the solid more often.
cards.say: Why does warmer water dissolve a solid faster? Its particles move faster and hit the solid more often.

cards.front: Why does stirring help a solid dissolve faster?
cards.back: It moves the dissolved solute away from the solid, so fresh water can touch it.
cards.say: Why does stirring help a solid dissolve faster? It moves the dissolved solute away from the solid, so fresh water can touch it.

cards.front: Why does crushing a sugar lump help it dissolve faster?
cards.back: Crushing makes more of the sugar touch the water at once.
cards.say: Why does crushing a sugar lump help it dissolve faster? Crushing makes more of the sugar touch the water at once.

cards.front: saturated solution
cards.back: A solution in which no more solute can dissolve at that temperature.
cards.say: saturated solution. A solution in which no more solute can dissolve at that temperature.

cards.front: How can you get salt back from salty water?
cards.back: Heat the solution gently so the water evaporates. The salt is left behind.
cards.say: How can you get salt back from salty water? Heat the solution gently so the water evaporates. The salt is left behind.

cards.front: Is dissolving the same as melting?
cards.back: No. Melting is a solid changing to a liquid when heated. Dissolving needs a liquid to mix the solid into.
cards.say: Is dissolving the same as melting? No. Melting is a solid changing to a liquid when heated. Dissolving needs a liquid to mix the solid into.

cards.front: Is water the only solvent?
cards.back: No. Other liquids can be solvents too. Nail varnish remover dissolves nail varnish.
cards.say: Is water the only solvent? No. Other liquids can be solvents too. Nail varnish remover dissolves nail varnish.

cards.front: Does flour dissolve in water?
cards.back: No. It makes a cloudy mixture and slowly settles, so flour is insoluble.
cards.say: Does flour dissolve in water? No. It makes a cloudy mixture and slowly settles, so flour is insoluble.

cards.front: Does cooking oil dissolve in water?
cards.back: No. The oil floats on top of the water.
cards.say: Does cooking oil dissolve in water? No. The oil floats on top of the water.

cards.front: You test how fast sugar dissolves in warm and cold water. What must stay the same?
cards.back: The amount of water, the amount of sugar, the size of the sugar pieces and the amount of stirring.
cards.say: You test how fast sugar dissolves in warm and cold water. What must stay the same? The amount of water, the amount of sugar, the size of the sugar pieces and the amount of stirring.
